where: The composed filled document carried the table's raw custodial account id in three places: household.accounts[].account_id, the keys of each account-grain by_row member (for example pvs.ytd.ending_value), and the names of chart lines that are an account.
rule: Each raw account id of the household is replaced by ids.opaque_account(firm, raw), the handler's own minted id, in account_id, in the by_row keys equal to a raw id and in the chart line names equal to a raw id; the asset-class keys such as equity, bonds and cash, a line such as Total and every other key or name stay as composed, and the account order stays the one _filled_compose made (sorted by the raw id before minting).
words: The reader now returns the document with its account ids minted. A new private helper, _filled_mint, in the first FILLED-REPORT-A block runs on the output of _filled_compose inside read_filled_report_gold and replaces each raw custodial id of the household with ids.opaque_account(firm, raw), the same minted form the summary builder and the directory carry. It changes account_id in household.accounts, the keys of every by_row member whose key is one of those raw ids, and the names of every chart line whose name is one of them. Class keys such as equity, bonds and cash, a line such as Total, and every other key stay as composed, and the account order is the one _filled_compose made. _filled_compose, _filled_partition_index, publisher.py and locals.tf are unchanged. Seven existing reader tests now expect the minted form through a helper, and five new tests carry mint in their names. NOT proven: nothing was deployed or invoked, the FILLED_REPORT_PASS switch stays off, no AWS call was made, and whether every real by_row member of the real filled_report_values table is keyed by an account or by a class was not read here.
